topSignals.title: FuelCell Energy + Siemens MoU (July 9) — first appearance in digest
topSignals.text: — FCEL and Siemens signed a non-binding MoU on July 9, 2026 to co-develop distributed fuel cell power systems for 100 MW+ data center projects. Siemens provides the electrical balance-of-plant (medium-voltage switchgear, microgrid controls, protection relays, SCADA) that data center operators require; FCEL supplies the fuel cell modules. The architecture leverages Siemens's installed base of ~600 GW of global power infrastructure, potentially accelerating FCEL's route to large data center operators who already use Siemens electrical systems. The MoU followed the Hunterbrook/scandium attack on Bloom the same day — giving FCEL a positive catalyst on a difficult day for the sector. GlobeNewswire | DCD | Siemens

topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4 abeyance deadline passed August 3 — decision imminent
topSignals.text: — All six RTOs/ISOs had until August 3 to file for a 90-day abeyance under FERC's June 18 show cause orders. No public FERC response is visible as of August 4. Commission has stated it will "heavily scrutinize" requests and disfavor extensions. If any abeyance is denied: the August 17 tariff-reform hard deadline activates immediately. If granted: November 16 stakeholder filing deadline. This decision directly triggers or defers the $5–20/MWh avoided-transmission-cost LCOE credit for on-site SOFC projects in PJM, MISO, CAISO, ISO-NE, NYISO, and SPP. Watch ferc.gov/rm26-4 today. FERC RM26-4 docket | McGuireWoods analysis

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy scandium class action reaches geopolitical risk mainstream
topSignals.text: — The D&O Diary published "Geopolitical Issues Lead to Securities Suit Against Fuel Cell Company" in August 2026, framing Bloom's scandium class action as a precedent-setting case for fuel cell manufacturers under securities law. The underlying issue: Hunterbrook's July 8 report traced four China-linked routes into Bloom's scandium supply (direct shipments to its Delaware plant plus ceramics and powders via Thailand, Japan, and South Korea intermediaries). Bloom denied the allegations. The class action (Robbins LLP, Kaplan Fox; Northern District of California) covers buyers of Bloom securities between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026; lead plaintiff deadline September 28, 2026. The D&O Diary notes this may be the first fuel cell case driven by geopolitical rare earth supply chain risk rather than product failure — with potential disclosure implications for all SOFC manufacturers using scandium-stabilized zirconia electrolytes. D&O Diary | TipRanks | Robbins LLP

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new announcements August 4. Status from August 3: E3000 G2 EFCF 2026 paper now accessible on ResearchGate — >75% FC electrical efficiency (stack-level), 90% total with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 in SOEC mode, zero degradation across 23,000 rapid current cycles, performance improvement in electrolysis mode. ELCO I Tallinn factory (360 MW/yr) in production and delivering G2 stacks. Next watch: full peer-reviewed paper and system-boundary efficiency confirmation at production scale (stack-only LHV vs. net system electrical). Elcogen E3000 G2 | ResearchGate paper

Topsoe (priority): Quiet day. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory (500 MW/yr) hibernated pending commercial-scale H2 demand. SOFC/data-center pathway deferred to 2029+. CEO Elena Scaltritti (since June 1, 2026). FY2026 guidance DKK 7,600–8,400M revenue, EBIT margin 4–9%. Topsoe investor relations
Other players: Quiet day. No new announcements from Bloom (technology), Ceres Power, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, or new entrants.

FuelCell Energy + Siemens MoU (July 9, first appearance) — See Top Signal #1. Non-binding MoU targets 100 MW+ co-developed systems combining FCEL fuel cell modules with Siemens electrical BOP, battery energy storage, and microgrid controls. Jointly designed for data centers and industrial offtakers in power-constrained markets. FCEL's 12.5 MW packaged power block (ten 1.25 MW modules) is the primary product unit; Siemens provides the electrical integration layer. GlobeNewswire | Data Center Frontier

Active pipeline unchanged: Oracle/Jupiter (2.45 GW NM, air permit public hearing Oct 19, NM AG investigation ongoing), Crusoe/Cheyenne (900 MW Phase 1 Bloom SOFCs), FCEL/Fit Energy (380 MW total, 30 MW initial delivery H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW across 19+ DCs, Bloom/Brookfield $25B, Nebius 328 MW EaaS.

FERC RM26-4 — abeyance decision imminent — See Top Signal #2. All six RTO/ISO abeyance requests filed by August 3. FERC decision expected this week. If denied: August 17 tariff reform hard deadline activates; RTOs/ISOs must file tariff revisions enabling expedited interconnection for co-located/self-supply large loads. If granted (90 days): November 16. For SOFC LCOE model: hold $5–20/MWh avoided-T-cost as a conditional input until outcome is published. FERC RM26-4

Background unchanged: NY state 50 MW+ grid interconnection moratorium (islanded exemption active); EU CADA data center energy efficiency rating scheme still under development (missed Q2 deadline); Germany EnEfG PUE ≤1.2 / ERF ≥10% / 15% waste heat reuse effective July 2026.

Bloom Energy (BE): August 3 close $218.32 (+6.08% from $205.81); intraday range $191.00–$224.64. Recovery continues from July 31 intraday trough of $159.80 (post-Q2 earnings selloff combined with scandium class action news). BE +460% over 52 weeks but down ~29% in the past month. 29-analyst consensus PT $273.51 (implied +25% upside from $218). Q2 2026 (reported July 28): record revenue $1.07B, operating income $182.2M (vs. operating loss prior year). FY2026 guidance raised: $3.9–4.2B revenue (+100% at midpoint), $2.55–2.85 non-GAAP EPS, $800–900M operating income. Q3 2026 earnings (October) next catalyst. Scandium class action lead plaintiff deadline: September 28, 2026. CNBC | StockAnalysis.com

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): ~$21.60 (August 2 last confirmed close). $225M upsized equity offering (July 7–8) overhang persists. FCEL + Siemens MoU (July 9) not yet translated to a stock catalyst. Q3 FY2026 earnings (October). Analyst range: B. Riley Buy $32 | Jefferies Buy $24 | UBS Neutral $22. CNBC

Ceres Power (LON: CWR): ~292 GBp, no material update since August 3. ~-40% from June peak. First royalties received from licensees (Doosan commercial-scale manufacturing active); H1 2026 results (September) are the next catalyst and first-royalties commercial confirmation. Ceres Power newsroom

SOFC-GT automated configuration synthesis achieving 72.64% system efficiency (Energy, 2026): New paper published March 23, 2026 in Energy journal: "Automated configuration synthesis of solid oxide fuel cell – gas turbine (SOFC-GT) hybrid systems: A fuel-syngas block state-mapping approach under SOFC safety constraints" demonstrates that an automated multi-pressure SOFC-GT configuration synthesis approach raises overall system efficiency from 66.10% to 72.64% (9.89% relative improvement). The method applies a fuel-syngas block state-mapping approach under SOFC safety constraints to identify optimal SOFC-GT integration configurations. LCOE flag: If reproducible at commercial scale, this represents ~+6.5 ppt net electrical efficiency vs. the 66.10% baseline — translating to significant fuel cost savings. ScienceDirect

Scandium supply chain risk — D&O Diary August 2026: The D&O Diary article establishes that SOFC manufacturers using scandium-doped zirconia electrolytes may face enhanced securities disclosure obligations regarding rare earth sourcing geography. First precedent of its kind in the fuel cell sector. D&O Diary

SOFC-GT automated configuration synthesis (Energy, March 2026) — See Research & IP above. System-level SOFC-GT integration study: automated state-space search over SOFC safety constraints identifies multi-pressure configurations achieving 72.64% system efficiency. Directly relevant to SOFC-GT CHP for data centers where waste heat recovery is a primary value lever alongside firm 24/7 power. ScienceDirect
Quiet day otherwise. No new system-level SOFC TEA/LCOE papers or preprints identified for August 4.

lcoe.text: BE Q2 2026 confirmed ($1.07B revenue, $182.2M operating income): Record quarter confirms backlog-to-revenue conversion at scale. FY2026 guidance $3.9–4.2B implies demand is running ahead of manufacturing capacity (Fremont 2 GW ramp not complete). Implication: system capex reduction may lag manufacturing scale; maintain $5,800–6,500/kW as base-case system capex for H2 2026, with 2027 downside sensitivity at ~$4,500/kW once Fremont ramp completes.

SOFC-GT hybrid efficiency 72.64% (new paper): At ~+6.5 ppt net electrical efficiency vs. 66.10% baseline, a SOFC-GT hybrid using the optimized multi-pressure configuration saves approximately $15–20/MWh in fuel costs at $6/MMBtu gas vs. a standalone SOFC. Flag as a "SOFC-GT hybrid" sensitivity case in LCOE model; apply only to projects with thermal integration infrastructure (district heat, industrial process heat, or steam turbine bottoming cycle).

FERC RM26-4 avoided-T-cost (decision pending): Maintain $5–20/MWh as conditional LCOE placeholder. If abeyance denied: activate as live input for PJM/MISO/CAISO/ISO-NE regions — adds $5–20/MWh economic advantage to on-site SOFC vs. grid-connected generation. If granted: defer to November 16.

Scandium supply chain premium risk: If disclosure requirements tighten following the Bloom class action precedent, SOFC manufacturers may need to source non-China scandium. Current market premium for ex-China scandium oxide: estimated 20–40% above Chinese spot price (~$1,800–2,000/kg Chinese spot; ~$2,200–2,800/kg ex-China). At ~1–2 kg scandium per kW SOFC stack, this adds ~$2,200–5,600/kW incremental material cost in a worst-case non-China sourcing scenario. Flag as a tail-risk sensitivity input, not a base-case assumption.

Pending (carry-forward): FERC RM26-4 outcome (today/tomorrow). Bloom 10-Q (due September 11 = 45 days from July 28) for explicit shipped MW and revenue-per-kW. Elcogen E3000 G2 system-level efficiency confirmation at ELCO I production scale.
